reviewer_round8_fixes: P1-1 (authority.py legacy idempotency key): f'{plan_id}:{version}' could violate the contract 16–128 length rule because plan_id has no bounded length and PublisherService.publish does not re-run the input schema, so an illegal key would land in idempotency_registry verbatim. Replaced with _legacy_publish_key = 'legacy-publish-' + sha256(canonical([plan_id, version])) — fixed 79-char length for ANY plan_id, deterministic per binding (case A replay preserved), separator-injection-safe. Regression tests: 1-char id, 5000-char id, same-binding determinism, version sensitivity, 'A:1'@2 vs 'A'@1 non-collision, stored registry key bounds, replay returns the original receipt (tests/unit/test_runtime_authority.py, 2 new tests)

P1-2 (api_server.py object guard): the pre-dispatch 'request body must be an object' bare-400 guard ran BEFORE middleware.execute, so array/string/number/null bodies on /publish bypassed the contract envelope, got no INVALID_INPUT/retryable/correlation_id/details and produced no observer trace. /publish now passes ANY parsed JSON value (refs={} for non-mappings) into the shared middleware; only the legacy routes keep the object guard. HTTP test pins all four non-object bodies -> 400 + INVALID_INPUT tool_error + exactly one trace + zero writes (tests/unit/test_p2_5_http_publish.py, 1 new test)

Evidence wording (both points corrected here and in the devlog entry): the actor claim now states audit-record truth (receipt/trace carry no actor field; the receipt binds via audit_log_id); the STATE_NOT_FOUND->409 correction is no longer code-only — the §6.3 table in .kiro/specs/publisher-transaction/design.md now lists STATE_NOT_FOUND in the 409 row, so design and code agree
